title: Serre regularity from finite residue-field projective dimension
statement: Let R be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with residue field k. If k has projective dimension at most n for some natural number n [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension], then R is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Serre theorem of_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_residueField and its auxiliary proof, lines 446-556; statement also Stacks 00OC (1) => (3).

proof.text: Use the already proved source declaration of_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_residueField, whose auxiliary theorem inducts strongly on e = spanFinrank(m). The complete argument is as follows. If m = 0, the generator criterion makes R regular.

If m contains no nonzerodivisor, the annihilator lemma gives s != 0 killing m. The source lemma free_of_hasProjectiveDimensionLE_of_annihilator, by induction on projective dimension and tensoring kernel inclusions with k, makes k free. In a basis of this nonzero free R-module, multiplication by y in m is zero; a basis coordinate then gives y = 0. Thus m = 0, the preceding case.

Otherwise prime avoidance for the finitely many associated primes, together with Nakayama for m^2, supplies a nonzerodivisor x in m outside m^2. Put S = R/(x); it is nontrivial Noetherian local. The two spanFinrank inequalities in the source show spanFinrank(m_S) + 1 = e.

The short exact sequence 0 -> m -> R -> k -> 0 gives pd_R(m) <= n by dimension shifting (use the weakened bound pd_R(k) <= n+1). Change of rings for the regular element x gives pd_S(S tensor_R m) <= n. The source nonempty_retract_residueField lemma for x outside m^2 makes the residue field of S a retract of S tensor_R m, so its projective dimension is also at most n.

Apply the induction hypothesis to S. Regularity gives spanFinrank(m_S) = dim S, and the nonzerodivisor dimension inequality gives dim S + 1 <= dim R. Hence spanFinrank(m_R) <= dim R and R is regular by the generator criterion. This proof is independent of the Koszul lower bound being proved by the parent.
